title: The Microchip DMAC G2 driver does not copy the new descriptor into the write-back descriptor in dma_mchp_config, so dma_get_status can report a stale pending length after configuration.
summary: On 2026-05-11 the G1 driver (dma_mchp_dmac_g1.c) was fixed to copy the source address, destination address and beat count of the freshly built descriptor into the write-back descriptor in dma_mchp_config and in reload, because dma_get_status reads the remaining length from the write-back descriptor whenever the channel is not the active one. The G2 driver already does this copy in dmac_desc_reload_block, but its dma_mchp_config still stops after dma_mchp_desc_setup without touching descriptors_wb[channel]. As a result, a dma_get_status call on G2 after dma_config, while the channel is not the active one, returns the beat count left in the write-back area by an earlier transfer (zero at boot) instead of the newly configured length, which is the 'stale pending_length' the commit message describes and can mislead callers that compute transferred bytes from pending_length. The fix is to add the same three assignments (plus the typed desc/desc_wb pointers) after dma_mchp_desc_setup in G2's dma_mchp_config; the multi-block check from the same hunk set is already present in G2, so only part of the picked change is needed.

subject: drivers: flash: stm32: xspi: fix XSPI page layout fallback
label: missing
evidence: The XSPI hunk replaces `erase_size = BIT(value)` plus the `if (erase_size == 0)` fallback with `(value != 0U) ? title: The STM32 OSPI flash driver never falls back to the 4 KiB sector size in its page layout when the flash reports no erase type, because BIT(0) is 1, not 0.
summary: On 2026-09-16 (commit 0b92a79e) the STM32 XSPI flash driver fixed setup_pages_layout so that, when no erase type is found, the layout uses SPI_NOR_SECTOR_SIZE instead of a one-byte erase size. The STM32 OSPI driver has the same function with the old code: it computes BIT(value) and only falls back when the result is 0, which never happens. When the flash's SFDP tables leave no erase type, the OSPI page layout reports the 256-byte program page as the erase page, while the driver's erase function refuses any size that is not a multiple of 4 KiB. Code that erases one layout page at a time through the flash page layout would then get an error. The change is a one-line copy with the same names.

title: The MAX32 RTIO I2C driver never completes a zero-length transfer whose address is ACKed, so "i2c scan" and any other 0-length write hang forever.
summary: Commit 7ae44ec850 (2025-04) fixed i2c_max32.c so that its controller ISR releases the waiting thread when a target ACKs its address and the message carries no data, which stopped "i2c scan" from looping forever in interrupt mode. The RTIO variant i2c_max32_rtio.c, built instead of i2c_max32.c when CONFIG_I2C_RTIO is enabled, still has the old ADDR_ACK branch, and none of its other completion paths fire for a message with no data, so such a transfer is never completed. The caller then blocks forever in rtio_submit() while holding the bus lock, so the scan stops at the first device that answers and every later transfer on that I2C controller also blocks. The port has to be adapted: the RTIO driver signals completion with complete_flag and max32_complete() instead of a semaphore, and probably needs to issue the STOP itself. Separately, max32_complete() already returns without completing anything when the bus runs at the standard-speed clock setting (line 319), so this gap is what blocks the scan at the other speeds; none of this has been confirmed on hardware.

label: unsure
evidence: The picked hunks wire a per-instance PM notifier into the EUSART init macro; the notifier disables TX/RX before EM2/EM3 and re-enables them after, because, in the fix's words, "EUSART instances in power domain PD1 are not EM2-capable: their clock is gated in EM2, and if the transmitter or receiver is left enabled across the sleep, the transceiver FIFO state is corrupted", and it follows "the EM2 entry sequence documented for the peripheral" using EUSART-only constructs (EUSART_EM2_CAPABLE(EUSART_NUM(...)), EUSART_SYNCBUSY_TXDIS, EUSART_STATUS_TXENS). uart_silabs_usart.c drives a different peripheral through em_usart.h and is structurally like the pre-fix EUSART driver: it only takes PM locks during active transfers, its data struct has no notifier, and it disables the USART only on device-PM SUSPEND, so an idle enabled instance can enter EM2 with TX/RX on. label: missing
evidence: The fix makes the two callback setters exclusive because, per the commit, "having callbacks on both API would interfere with each other in almost all cases"; the CONFIG_UART_EXCLUSIVE_API_CALLBACKS option it adds (still present, default y, depends on UART_ASYNC_API && UART_INTERRUPT_DRIVEN) documents that "calling uart_callback_set() would disable the callback previously set via uart_irq_callback_set()". uart_bee.c implements both APIs (Kconfig.bee selects SERIAL_SUPPORT_INTERRUPT and SERIAL_SUPPORT_ASYNC, the API table has both .irq_callback_set and .callback_set) and uses the very same field names as uart_stm32.c, but uart_bee_irq_callback_set() (lines 432-433) and uart_bee_async_callback_set() (lines 494-495) only store their own callback, and nothing else in the file ever clears user_cb or async_cb. Its ISR has the same shape as the pre-fix STM32 one: uart_bee_isr() calls data->user_cb whenever it is set and then runs the async RX-idle handling, so a leftover interrupt-driven callback keeps running during async transfers. The generic wrappers in include/zephyr/drivers/uart/uart_internal.h just forward to the driver, so nothing outside the driver enforces exclusivity; maintainers still treat the omission as a defect (2026 commit 1718448d76 "silabs_eusart: Respect exclusive API callbacks").
title: The Realtek Bee UART driver does not clear the other API's callback when one is set, so the interrupt-driven and async callbacks can both stay active even though exclusive callbacks are enabled by default.
summary: In 2022 commit 9f02eead added CONFIG_UART_EXCLUSIVE_API_CALLBACKS (default y when both the interrupt-driven and async APIs are enabled) and changed drivers such as uart_stm32.c so that setting the IRQ callback clears the async callback and vice versa. The Realtek Bee driver received its async API in August 2026 (eb525902e0) with the same field names (user_cb/user_data, async_cb/async_user_data), but uart_bee_irq_callback_set() and uart_bee_async_callback_set() still only store the new callback. Because uart_bee_isr() calls the interrupt-driven callback on every UART interrupt before handling async RX idle, a callback installed earlier (for example by a console or shell) keeps running during async transfers and can read or react to data meant for the DMA receiver, against the documented Kconfig behaviour. The problem only shows when both APIs are used on the same UART instance; the four-line #if CONFIG_UART_EXCLUSIVE_API_CALLBACKS blocks from uart_stm32.c can be copied as is.

title: The STM32 I2C v2 RTIO driver does not hand an own-address match to target handling while its own controller START is still pending, so the target transfer is not serviced and the bus can hang.
summary: Commit dd9b1122e1 (2026-04-29) changed the non-RTIO STM32 I2C v2 driver so that an own-address match (ADDR) seen while the controller is marked active aborts the pending controller START and switches to target handling; follow-up 879678acbb for the same issue #99074 refined it, and neither touched the RTIO driver. i2c_stm32_v2_rtio.c, which drives the same v2 block, still sets controller_active before generating START, keeps the ADDR interrupt enabled while a target is registered, and its event ISR only goes to target handling when controller_active is false, while its controller path never checks or clears ADDR. If another controller on the bus addresses this device while its own transfer is waiting to start, the target callbacks do not run and ADDR stays pending, which per the commit message 'may leave the bus stuck'. The port has to be adapted because the RTIO data structure has no current.is_arlo or device_sync_sem, so the aborted request must be completed through the RTIO completion path. This is from reading the code only; the race needs a multi-controller bus with a registered target and has not been reproduced.

title: The Broadcom PAX v1 DMA driver still starts at the generic DMA init priority, before the PCIe endpoint it requires, so its init fails or the default init-priority check rejects the build.
summary: In July 2023 the PAX v2 DMA driver got its own init priority symbol (default 51) so that it starts after the iProc PCIe endpoint driver it depends on through the pcie-ep phandle. The PAX v1 driver, which had the same code at that time, still uses CONFIG_DMA_INIT_PRIORITY (default 40) while the PCIe endpoint driver starts at 50, and its init function returns -ENODEV when the endpoint is not yet initialized. On a board that uses the v1 compatible, the default build-time priority check would reject the build, and with that check off the DMA device would fail to initialize at boot. The port is the same Kconfig symbol under a v1 name used in v1's device definition. No in-tree devicetree enables brcm,iproc-pax-dma-v1, so only out-of-tree boards are affected, which is why confidence is medium.

title: The MAX32 I3C controller fails to initialize when the devicetree omits i2c-scl-hz or i3c-scl-hz, because init never fills in default SCL rates.
summary: In 2024 the NXP MCUX I3C driver was fixed to fill in default I2C and I3C SCL rates in its init function when the devicetree leaves them out, because its configure function rejects a zero rate and init otherwise failed. The MAX32 I3C driver, added in 2025, has the same structure: the rates come from DT_INST_PROP_OR(..., 0), max32_i3c_configure returns -EINVAL for a zero rate, and max32_i3c_init calls it without setting any defaults. On a board or overlay that enables the MAX32 I3C controller without both rate properties, which the binding allows and says should mean the controller default, the controller fails to initialize and the bus is unusable. The NXP HAL default-config call does not exist for MAX32 and the MAX32 HAL is not in this repository, so the port has to choose default rates itself. The in-tree max32657evkit board sets both properties, so it is not affected today.

summary: The Andes ATCSPI200 SPI driver was fixed in commit f817f62021 (merged 2025-07-31): full-duplex transfers are now sized by MAX of the TX and RX lengths, with exact TX/RX frame counters so the shorter side is padded with dummy frames, because the IP needs equal write and read counts; the same commit also corrected how chained DMA blocks are counted. The Egis ET171 driver, whose binding and Kconfig say it is based on the ATCSPI200, was added on 2025-08-16 with the older code: transceive() still uses MIN(rx_len, tx_len), programs that one count into both transfer counters, and finishes the transaction at the END interrupt. A call such as a register-address write followed by a longer read therefore clocks only the shorter length and returns success, leaving the rest of the RX buffer unfilled (or the extra TX bytes unsent), and the DMA reload callbacks and chained block count still follow the old logic.
